title: I Closed the Barista Shift With the Tip Jar Policy They Wrote

parts.text: I counted the tip jar into a labeled envelope and watched my manager pocket a five because it. The cafe smelled like burnt oat milk and wet cardboard sleeves. My manager, Chelsea, had posted a new policy: misshapen bills are store property until verified. She had written it after a customer left a twenty with a phone number. "This one's creased," she said, holding my five. I said, "It's a five." She smiled. "Policy." The regular, Mr. Ortiz, always orders a cortado and leaves coins that smell like his pocket. He asked, "You okay, Priya?" I said, "Ask Chelsea about creases." Chelsea laughed for him. "Jokes." After close I photographed the policy on the fridge, the one under a magnet from a dairy vendor. I also photographed the envelope total versus the POS tip line. They did not match by thirty-five dollars, all of it "creased." My coworker Jonah arrived for close. "She's been doing the fold thing since summer," he said. Chelsea overheard from the office. "If you want Sunday hours, you'll verify with me." Sunday hours were how I paid rent. I needed them. I also needed the five. Then the owner, a man named Vic who only appears for health inspections, walked in because the health inspector was tomorrow. Chelsea dropped my five into the register like it had always lived there. Vic looked at the fridge. "What's misshapen bills?" he asked, and the dairy magnet slid down an inch.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The owner is reading her crease policy the night before a health inspection, and my five is in the register.

social.video_title: She pocketed tips for being creased — Part 1/2
social.description: Burnt oat milk, a dairy magnet, and a policy invented for a twenty with a phone number. Sunday hours were the leverage. Would you have photographed the fridge?

parts.text: I said, "It's how creased tips become store property." Vic asked Chelsea if payroll knew. She said it was temporary. I showed the POS photo. Jonah, shaking, showed a note on his phone with dates. Vic is not a hero. He is a man afraid of inspectors and wage claims on the same weekend. He had Chelsea put the thirty-five in the envelope. He took the fridge policy down. The magnet left a clean rectangle. I still did not get automatic Sunday hours. I picked them up because Jonah quit two weeks later and someone had to open. Chelsea got "retraining." She still watches folds. I crease nothing on purpose now, which is petty, and I put coins from Mr. Ortiz in a separate cup so they don't vanish into verification. Vic wrote a real tip policy: all tips split by hours, no manager discretion. I printed it and taped it where the magnet was. The oat milk still burns if you walk away. I walk away less. When students ask if the job is chill, I say count your envelope before the office door closes. They think I am cynical. I am just good at cardboard sleeves and math.

social.video_title: The clean rectangle on the fridge was the policy — Part 2/2
social.description: Wage-claim weekend energy put the thirty-five back. The dairy magnet left a pale square. Would you have creased nothing on purpose after that?
